summary: Defined and implemented the conservative Search predicate acceptance matrix, preserving residual SQL semantics while filtering accepted predicates at the owning source row boundary.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning repository's Search planner, accepted-row filtering seams, predicate tests and predicate-planning documentation changed, plus this scope's campaign evidence. No sibling repository, public constructor signature, package version or publication state changed.
implementation.matrix: Matches, lines, files, counts and paths accept only their declared scalar metadata columns. Equality, ordered comparison, literal-member IN/NOT IN, IS NOT NULL and supported AND/OR forms are evaluated; unsupported OR and generic NOT remain residual, and normal search.many remains reject-all.
implementation.semantics: Accepted predicates are copied identically into the source result and execution plan. Alias and case normalization, ordinal strings, invariant numeric conversion, reverse operands and SQL three-valued NULL behavior are preserved. Row filtering does not renumber match or line coordinates, and counts are filtered only after complete per-file accumulation.
implementation.differentialEvidence: Baseline source execution and accepted-predicate execution agree for matches, lines, files, counts and paths, including the compiled outer-join regression.

gateResults.evidence: The exact Release suite exited 0 across 21 projects with 1,517 total tests, 1,483 passed, 0 failed and 34 classified skips; the Search suite and eight predicate-planning tests also passed.

The separate ownership review approved the predicate matrix, residual boundary, SQL NULL behavior, join safety and scope boundary; exact commands, tool versions, source/artifact hashes and the unique trailer-bearing completion commit are retained.
Focused tests cover accepted and residual partitioning, aliases, reverse comparisons, invariant conversions, SQL UNKNOWN, all normal Search row shapes and compiled outer-join NULL extension.

The Search planner carries identical accepted predicates in the source result and execution plan, the accepted-row seams compile for normal Search shapes, and the warnings-as-errors Search build passed.

knownLimitations: The accepted metadata predicate is a row-level filter and does not prune filesystem traversal or content opening.

The normal search.many planner boundary remains reject-all; explicit accepted plans are consumed by the source, while ordinary many-pattern pushdown requires a later scope with join and correlation qualification.
IS NULL remains residual because the provider has no join nullability context; ordinary NULL comparisons and NULL-containing NOT IN preserve SQL UNKNOWN semantics.
The evaluator supports the scalar types present in Search rows; unsupported forms and incompatible non-numeric pairs remain residual or evaluate as UNKNOWN.
